next_step: Finalize throughput SLA terms and sign MSA; legal to review SLA penalties
notes:
Account snapshot: enterprise payments platform; PCI-adjacent workflows (no card PAN storage in ML stack), heavy spikes during payroll windows and end-of-day reconciliation. Primary ask: predictable, contract-backed throughput guarantees with clear concurrency and burst rules.

Recent timeline and irreversible bullets: 
- 2026-02-11: Intro call (AE Maya + SE Oliver) — high-level scope, told them Redwood dedicated fits our isolation needs. CTO asked about tokens/sec baseline.
- 2026-02-18: Security deep-dive (security PM + Redwood security SME) — KMS + audit requirements; flagged HSM integration for keys.
- 2026-02-25: Tech workshop / perf proof-of-concept kickoff (SE-led). Run plan: synthetic throughput run + replay of 48h peak telemetry.
- 2026-03-02: POC results review (Fireflies FF-20260212-8234). Redwood baseline: 9.8k sustained tokens/sec with p95 latency 160ms on quantized variant; 13.6k tokens/sec on larger replica with H100s but tail spikes observed.
- 2026-03-05: Commercial sync — procurement asks for guaranteed minimum and clear credit/penalty schedule.
- 2026-03-09: SLA draft v2 shared (drive link).

Use-case / requirements (customer language + shorthand):
- "Payroll windows are non-negotiable — we cannot have higher latency or token throttling when millions of instructions are processed." — VP Eng.
- Workload: mixture of short transactional prompts (8-64 tokens) + embedding batches (1k queries/min bursts) + rerank jobs for reconciliation.
- Targets requested: minimum sustained throughput 10,000 tokens/sec (global, across reserved fleet), concurrency cap handling up to 500 concurrent inference sessions, p95 latency SLO <= 200ms for 128-token responses.
- Burst policy ask: tolerate short bursts to 30-40% above committed throughput for up to 5 minutes per 1-hour window; prefer auto-burst into a paid overage rather than hard throttling.

Reserved GPU planning (customer preference + negotiation notes):
- Starting proposal: 8 x H100-80GB reserved in NA region, with 2x autoscale buffer GPUs for short bursts. Customer asked for a proposal with A100-80GB alternative to reduce cost.
- SE note: H100 gives better perf for long-context / KV-heavy workloads; A100 quantized path improves unit-cost but increases p95 by ~20ms.
- Request: explicit mapping in contract of reserved GPU count -> guaranteed tokens/sec (i.e., 8 H100 => min 10k tokens/sec sustained; list exact config).

Throughput SLA negotiation points (open / items to close):
- Measurement window: customer insists on 15-minute rolling windows for SLA evaluation (Redwood default is 5/1m in some docs). Need to align.
- Credit formula: customer requests service credits equal to 5% of monthly fees per percentage point below SLA up to cap. Legal wants cap at 50% — commercial to agree range.
- Concurrency accounting: define whether multi-tenant batch jobs count as "concurrency" or are billed as throughput usage only.
- Burst enforcement: prefer soft bursts (billing overage) vs hard throttles; need clear pre-warm rules.
- Fallback behavior: when capacity constrained, route to quantized variant (lower cost) with explicit quality delta; customer requires alerting and configurable tolerance thresholds.

POC / technical action items: 
- Run 24h replay at 1.5x recorded peak with both model families (Llama-family quantized, and larger open model) — deliver token/sec curves and p95/p99 latency. (Oliver)
- Provide formal mapping of reserved GPUs -> guaranteed tokens/sec and per-request concurrency assumptions. (Redwood product)
- Add clause for burst allowances with explicit billing/credit language and rehydration/pre-warm time. (AE + Commercial)

Commercial notes / asks from customer: 
- Wants 12-month committed contract with quarterly performance reviews.
- Prefers usage-pegged overage billing (i.e., pay for burst tokens at negotiated rate) rather than site-wide throttles.
- Asks for a 30-day SLA measurement trial before finalizing credits wording.

Open risks / internal: 
- Procurement timeline aggressive: legal wants final SLA text by 2026-05-01.
- KMS/HSM integration might push to Private deployment if vendor HSM compliance fails. That changes economics.
- Accuracy regressions if routing to quantized fallback; product to provide eval results on sample prompt set.

Quotes / call snippets: 
- "We need hard guarantees for throughput — it's a revenue window for us." — SVP Ops
- "If you can give a deterministic mapping (GPUs -> tokens/sec) we can sign." — CTO

Next meeting: 2026-03-16 commercial + legal to resolve credit formula. Action owner list: Maya (commercial), Oliver (SE/Poc), Redwood product (SLA mapping), Legal (MSA redlines).
